`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Real `perf` sampling avoids the main weakness of the earlier profiling. GDB stack samples of release builds blame the wrong function when identical-code folding merges same-shaped functions. That gave two false hot spots in earlier work. `perf record` with call graphs samples far more often and pays no debugger overhead. During the Hiredis diagnosis, GDB overhead had inflated memory to about 3.65 GB.
- `perf_event_paranoid=1` allows user-space and kernel profiling of your own processes, but `/proc/kallsyms` stays restricted. So kernel frames show as raw addresses, and user-space Bifrost frames resolve normally.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

`perf` now works in this container, and I checked it myself: `perf stat`, `perf record` and `perf script` all give real samples. Kernel symbols are hidden, which doesn't matter for profiling Bifrost. I updated my profiling memory to say perf is available on the morannon Mjolnir container from today, and kept the older note about GDB sampling problems for other hosts. My workspace survived the container replacement: same branch, same head (`caf6cae25e`), and the grammar clone is intact.

Nothing is running, and the earlier question is still open. Every current real-repository case is parked behind larger gaps in what Bifrost's analysis can model:
- Rust: method-receiver resolution and Drop handling
- C/C++: unresolved local calls, cleanup and macros

Should I take on one of those, or move the campaign to cases with fewer blockers? Perf would help with either, for example in confirming the Hiredis scan's remaining 82–134 s cost.
